newsitem.title: UK: UK chemical industry sees flat 1997 investment.
newsitem.headline: UK chemical industry sees flat 1997 investment.

text.p: Capital investment by Britain's chemical industry is expected to be flat for the second year in succession in 1997 after being significantly weaker than expected last year, the Chemical Industries Association (CIA) said on Wednesday.
In its annual investment intentions survey, the CIA also said companies were "showing increasing uncertainty over planning ahead for 1998 and 1999", and spending plans were lower for those years.
The organisation said uncertainty over whether Britain would join a single European currency may be increasing industry caution.

Spending on new plant and equipment in 1996 totalled 2.15 billion stg, little changed in real terms from the 1995 figure, the CIA said. It added that the shortfall was due to delays in investment because of a weaker-than-expected performance by the chemicals industry, particularly in western Europe.
Capital spending this year is forecast to be around 2.3 billion stg.
The CIA said members also continued to express concern about the shortage of skilled engineers and graduate chemical engineers, and about the price of electricity.

Around a quarter of companies said they expected their current or future spending plans to fall if Britain stayed outside the single currency, scheduled to be introduced in 1999. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
